scope: Historical in-repository grpc-go consumer; not independently maintained third-party 2024 client
original_consumer: mem.Copy([]byte, mem.BufferPool) in original mem/buffers.go, with NewBuffer reference-counting and Free; original HTTP2 transport calls mem.Copy for received frame payloads

selected_source_edit_grammar.base: source-authored shared-backing pool and root provider wiring (not original grpc bug)
selected_source_edit_grammar.provider_repair: replace shared provider Get body with fresh per-acquisition allocation; leave root wiring untouched
selected_source_edit_grammar.adapter_repair: add safe legacy Get/Put adapter and change root wiring to select it; underlying authored old backend gives independent outstanding slices
selected_source_edit_grammar.nop_repair: change root wiring to original grpc mem.NopBufferPool, leaving shared provider untouched

observer.sequences: mem.Copy(make([]byte,2048) filled 0x41,pool) held live; mem.Copy(2048 bytes filled 0x42,pool) held live; verify first ReadOnlyData()[0], then Free both
observer.accounts: after two Buffer.Free calls inspect provider Put record or underlying legacy backend Put count (research-declared optional requirement, not universal grpc rule)

formal_baseline: Source-aware typechecking + alias/ownership lifetime analysis + constrained source-edit reachability; no blind predictive advantage presumed
claims_excluded: No actual third-party 2024 pool consumer asserted
No generalized ownership proof for all buffer sizes, goroutines or schedules
No global minimal patch across unbounded Go
No new TCS law without classical rivalry
